title: Heterogeneous-Quant Aware Kernel Planner and Capture Sanity Checker
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: reduce capture/replay correctness failures for multi-stream decodes when serving mixed-quant models and mixed-sequence workloads. Implement a kernel planning layer that is aware of per-layer quant profiles and attention kernel compatibility, and add a light-weight capture sanity checker (graph stamp + epoch fence) to detect and gracefully recover from nondeterministic graph divergence during replay. This reduces incidents where a stale cuda-graph or incompatible kernel variant causes KV mismatch or attention corruption at long sequence lengths.
updates: 2026-02-25: Initial proposal drafted — introduce an offline layer profiler that emits a per-model 'quant compatibility map' used by planner to prefer kernels with stable capture semantics.

2026-02-27: Spike completed — implemented prototype kernel-prober that runs micro-benchmarks to decide between fused attention and tiled attention kernels for quant-8 and q4f models. Observed 7-12% perf variance with different sequence lengths.

2026-03-01: Design decision — add a 16-byte 'graph stamp' placed in capture metadata and a monotonic 'KV epoch' written at prefill end to detect cross-stream divergence on replay. If mismatch, automatically fall back to interpreter decode path for that request and mark trace for further analysis.
2026-03-02: Integration PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842 — implements planner, stamp, and fallback path. Unit tests added for stamp mismatch and fallback instrumentation.

2026-03-03: Stress-run on internal dedicated pool (NVIDIA A100s) — reduced nondeterministic capture failures from ~0.6% to ~0.09% in mixed-quant workloads; observed +3ms median latency overhead when stamp checks enabled.
Next: finalize review feedback, add e2e regression tests with longer prefill windows, and tune planner heuristics for tail-latency-sensitive customers.
acceptance_criteria: Planner chooses stable kernel variants for at least 95% of model-layer combinations observed in production quant profiles without manual overrides
Capture sanity checker detects mismatches deterministically and triggers fallback; validated with injected divergence tests
No customer-facing correctness regression in A/B canary over 72h on dedicated pool
End-to-end telemetry added: per-request graph_stamp, kv_epoch, chosen_kernel, fallback_reason
testing_plan: Unit tests for kernel-prober and planner decision table
Fault injection test that flips a single kernel selection mid-capture to ensure stamp mismatch triggers fallback
Long-run canary: 7-day run on dedicated pool with mixed quant models (q4f, q8_0, q2) and sequence lengths up to 8k tokens
Add nightly regression that replays traces from known failure window and ensures deterministic replay after planner enabled
risks_and_mitigation: Increased tail latency from lightweight checks — mitigate by gating stamp checks behind 'safety:high' profile and adding sampling for lower tiers
Planner misclassification for new quant formats — mitigation: allow model pin overrides and ship a telemetry alert when unknown quant profile encountered
Complexity in release rollback — mitigation: feature flag with immediate kill-switch and metric-based auto-disable
